text: Normally that evidence disappears. When police search illegally, whatever they turn up is thrown out of the case.

text: The rule has exceptions. One is attenuation, when the link is so thinned out the connection barely holds.
provenance: But the rule has never been absolute.
The name for that idea is attenuation.
Attenuated just means thinned out, so far removed from the first mistake that the connection barely holds.

text: The warrant in Utah versus Strieff existed before the stop. It was valid and outstanding, so the search rode on it, not the stop.
provenance: That warrant existed before the detective ever stopped Strieff.
It was valid, it was outstanding, and it commanded the detective to make an arrest the moment it surfaced.
That search is legal on its own terms, because it rides on the warrant, not on the stop.

text: The stop was still illegal. The Court never pretended otherwise. It just stopped mattering to whether the drugs came into court.
